rationale: This is essentially the published asset-growth anomaly tilted by leverage (Cooper-Gulen-Schill interacted with the well-documented financing-friction conditioning of Li-Zhang / Lipson-Mortal-Schill), and because both terms are non-negative uniform ranks the product is dominated by the asset-growth main effect rather than any genuine interaction.

The indicator zeroes out every solvent firm, so the resulting sort is a mass of tied zeros (the majority of the cross-section) below all distressed firms — the portfolio is effectively a negative-retained-earnings dummy, not a capex×distress interaction, which contradicts the stated hypothesis and makes the long leg uninterpretable.

The capex-minus-operating-cash-flow funding gap crossed with a cash-to-current-liabilities buffer is an economically coherent and reasonably fresh construction (closer to Rajan-Zingales external finance dependence than to any single standard anomaly), though the rank-product form again loads heavily on the well-known external-financing main effect and should be diagnosed against that baseline.

target_name: Inventory Buildup Under Working Capital Strain
rationale: A defensible refinement of the Thomas-Zhang inventory-growth anomaly with a distinct liquidity mechanism, but note that inventory is itself a component of working capital, so the two legs are mechanically linked and the interaction will be attenuated — the test should confirm incremental power over plain inventory growth.

target_name: Disciplined Investment With Retained Earnings Strength
rationale: This is an additive (not interactive) combination of two directly published anomalies — asset growth and retained-earnings-to-assets — both of which are close proxies for the CMA and RMW factors that the FF5 benchmark already spans, so a meaningful alpha is unlikely and any finding would be a rediscovery.

The expression is internally inconsistent with its own reasoning: the product of two signed changes is equally large and positive for firms *cutting* capex while *delevering* (negative times negative) as for the escalating-commitment case the hypothesis targets, so the signal cannot separate the two states and the claimed long leg does not exist.
